title: Start the agent inside that folder
caption: Open the terminal in the extracted starter folder, check where you are, then start your AI agent: so it finds your workshop files.

windows.copilot: For Copilot, type pwsh in this window and press Enter first. This opens the PowerShell 7 installed earlier in the same folder.
windows.helpTitle: Didn't see “Open in Terminal”? Try this
windows.open: Open the extracted folder containing GLOSSARY.md in File Explorer. Press Ctrl+L, type the word shown below into the address bar, then press Enter.
windows.shellHint: Copilot uses pwsh for the PowerShell 7 installed earlier. If Windows cannot find it, stop and return to the installation step.
windows.check: Then check that you are in the right folder:
windows.location: The result must be the actual extracted starter folder, not your home folder or the ZIP. Your username and path can differ from the drawing.
windows.file: You see # hancrafted workshop starter. File not found? Open the folder containing GLOSSARY.md, not an outer folder. Do not start the agent until both checks work.
windows.fallback: Wrong location? In Explorer, open the actual folder containing GLOSSARY.md. Press Ctrl+L and copy its full path. In PowerShell, type Set-Location -LiteralPath , paste that path inside double quotes, then press Enter. Run Get-Location again. Do not paste the example username or assume your folder is in Downloads.

windows-folder.header: Check the folder, not the menu label
windows-folder.description: Microsoft documents launching PowerShell from Explorer's address bar [1]. Terminal hosts configurable shells, so Open in Terminal does not guarantee PowerShell 7 [2]. Get-Location checks the actual directory; Get-Content reads the starter file; Set-Location -LiteralPath accepts a literal path [3][4][5]. Microsoft's Windows 10 announcement documents the Shift-right-click PowerShell entry [6]; it does not guarantee that entry on every Windows 11 or managed machine. The menu and path drawings are examples. These routes have not been tested on current managed Windows machines.

agent-working-folder.header: A working folder is not a security boundary
agent-working-folder.description: The vendors instruct users to start in their project directory; Google documents agy as the CLI command [1][2]. The folder helps the agent discover the workshop's files and skills, but does not mean it can access only that directory. Approve only the intended workshop folder and review commands before allowing them.

open.title: Open a terminal in the folder

detail.mac: In Finder, right-click hancrafted-workshop-starter, then Services › New Terminal at Folder. No path to type.
detail.windows: In File Explorer, right-click the extracted hancrafted-workshop-starter folder and choose Open in Terminal. On Windows 10, hold Shift while you right-click and choose Open PowerShell window here.
detail.linux: Right-click the folder in your file manager › Open in Terminal. No path to type.

open.worked: The folder name hancrafted-workshop-starter appears before your cursor. Your username and the rest of the path may differ from the example.

note.mac: Not in the menu? Turn it on once: System Settings › Keyboard › Keyboard Shortcuts › Services, tick New Terminal at Folder.
note.windows: On Windows 10, or with an older menu, hold Shift while you right-click and choose Open PowerShell window here. Either opens PowerShell in this folder. The address-bar route needs neither menu entry.

start.title: Start your AI agent
start.detail: Type its name in this terminal and press Enter. If it asks whether you trust the folder, check the path: approve only the extracted starter folder.
start.antigravity: Start Antigravity in this folder as its official page shows.
start.worked: Your AI agent starts here for the first time and asks you to sign in. The next Slide walks you through it.

trust.question: Do you trust the files in this folder?

fallback.text: Fallback, if the menu won't work: open the terminal as in step 1, type <command></command> and press Enter.

go-in-then-start.title: Go in, then start
go-in-then-start.script: Start from the extracted starter folder. On Windows 11, right-click it and choose Open in Terminal; on Windows 10, hold Shift while you right-click and choose Open PowerShell window here. The menu drawing is an example; if yours has no such entry, open the help directly below it for another route. For Copilot, switch to the PowerShell 7 installed earlier by typing pwsh in that window first. Check that the prompt names the starter folder, then start your agent there: this is its very first start. If it asks whether you trust the folder, say yes, because this is the starter folder.

same-folder-every-time.title: Same folder every time
same-folder-every-time.script: The order matters because an AI agent reads what is in the folder it starts in. That is how it will find your skill in a moment, and if you start it somewhere else, the skill is simply not there. So whenever you work with this starter folder, start the AI agent from inside it.

chain-so-far.title: Chain so far
chain-so-far.script: Look at what you have. A terminal that waits, an AI agent inside it, and a folder it can read. One piece is left, and it is the one that proves all the others work.

notFound.title: Does it say “command not found” or “not recognized”?
notFound.fix: Close this window and open the terminal in the folder once more: a window opened before the install may not know the new command. Still not recognized? Return to the installation step and its version check: the install may have failed or PATH may need fixing. For a company policy or certificate error, stop and ask IT.
